state.case_summary:
A patient in their 70s presented with worsening shortness of breath, chest tightness, and episodes of palpitations. Medical history was remarkable for hypertension and kidney insufficiency.

Initial evaluation revealed:- Heart rate: 53 beats/min- Blood pressure: 221/85 mm Hg

- Laboratory tests:  * B-type natriuretic peptide: 838.6 pg/mL (normal level, <300 pg/mL)- ECG findings:  * Initial ECG:    Image Title: Initial 12-lead ECG    Image Description: Shows sinus bradycardia with prolonged P-wave duration (180 milliseconds), biphasic P wave morphology in leads II, III, and aVF, PR interval 280 milliseconds, QRS duration 120 milliseconds, rsR pattern in lead V1  * Follow-up ECG:    Image Description: Shows atrial flutter- Echocardiography:  * Left atrial enlargement (52 mm)  * Normal left ventricular wall thickness  * Mild pulmonary hypertension

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Atrial flutter with bradycardia
B. Bayés syndrome (Advanced interatrial block with paroxysmal atrial arrhythmias)
C. Atrial Flutter with Variable Block
D. Sick sinus syndrome
